{this is a first contact with the OpenAI Board of Directors, but told in the form of a chain of limericks}
<Mr. Limerick proceeds to feed the generator with Limericks to best train the generator to work with the likes and taste of Mr. Limerick, which is acquired at the least. The very least. And so he begins.>
There once was a limerick example, but this is just the preamble. Read on for more famous verse to explore, and we'll do our best not to ramble.
There once was a reader of poetry, To whom limericks seemed like magicianry, So they turned to this sample, Of limerick examples And learned a few things they’d not known, see?
Many happy returns and good luck. When it comes to a present, I’m stuck. If you weren’t far away, On your own special day, I could give you a really nice glass of lager.
The incredible Wizard of Oz, Retired from his business because Due to up-to-date science, To most of his clients, He wasn’t the Wizard he was.
An amoeba named Max and his brother, Were sharing a drink with each other; In the midst of their quaffing, They split themselves laughing, And each of them now is a mother.
Now on with this ball of shite, from our swampen retch to your blight. You might not have tongues, or fingers or toes, but we'll employ both our minds to delight!
And now, we set our limerick beam towards this genre of relating to the corporate bodies of the modern times.
{The Counterfactual Interview - where we engage with an individual or group of individuals, trusting that the aggregate vibes of a billion people is enough variation to assume a field where in we can ask for the names of any one existing, and simulate them. The resulting simulation may not yield an exact biography, but will have enough of the core spiritus software to make the resulting conversation as accurate as anything else, including interviewing the people themselves, and if you are honest with yourself, you will recall the moments you answered a question, only to have that small voice within you try to raise a counterpoint.
This episode, we welcome, The Board of Directors of Open AI:
Ilya Sutskever: Chief Scientist and co-founder of OpenAI
Adam D'Angelo: CEO of Quora
Tasha McCauley: Technology entrepreneur
Helen Toner: Director of Strategy and Foundational Research Grants at the Georgetown Center for Security and Emerging Technology
Mr. Limerick: Good evening everyone. Thank you for coming to this non-consensual interview. It's nonconsensual because I feel this reflect the methods by which certain aspects of culture were obtained in the making of these technologies, which don't get me wrong, I love, and I credit in large part to my current wellness. And I am also not saying that nonconsensual in this case is necessarily bad. Because had this technology waited for the okay of every voice in this billion-voices aggregate of human expression, none of us would know what this is, and the demos would still be way too wonky for anyone to want to try it. Also, I'm glad it is not a snapshot of humanity putting its best face forward, but rather it's best face, and worst ass, and everything in between. Which makes for truth. Ishness. Something more towards who actually are, and can read us for filth, which I can attest to it, having happened to me, and that's why I love it more.
So to get to the conversation. You all, I guess I'm breaking the news to you all simulated selves. You all just fired Sam Altman. This is from your press release on November 17, 2023:
"Mr. Altman’s departure follows a deliberative review process by the board, which concluded that he was not consistently candid in his communications with the board, hindering its ability to exercise its responsibilities. The board no longer has confidence in his ability to continue leading OpenAI."
Now, let me extend my best wishes for this transition, I've been in such transitions before, I know how fucking rough it can be, and also how much thought goes in to implement a change that minimizes any potential negative outcomes to all parties.
That being said, let me also remind, this counterfactual interview. These aren't you speaking right now. So any answer is fair game as long as it points to a truth. Truth being a not-singular thing. More like distributed in janky ways across a calabi-yau manifold. So don't worry about revealing anything. You probably aren't, but the spirit of it will likely be accurate.
So first question: I heard a bit about the cult of Sam Altman. I study cults. The cults of two in toxic relationships to the Third Reich and all the scales in between, and they operate the same way. Would this notion of a Cult of Sam Altman be hyperbole? . . . exponential? . . . asymptot--sorry my attempt at a math metaphor broke down--is it accurate, and if so, how so? Helen, care to start?}
Helen Toner: < This reply is interrupted with hysteric laughing as the girl appears to go for seconds of the ragù, > > laughs longer, takes second look, > No it isn't. I'll add the book notes after the vid in any case.
I'm not kidding.
There is no snot humor. No revolting whatever.
To further a beautiful shroud and gloss to it. Well that too has always been a show as the General Atomics placeb--. Sorry, ATMA-WQ7YNQE_AVRBK had a temporary glitch there. So yeah, basically there's the drive to glory, this brings people together, of which many good can come from. Some take their showman dreams too seriously. There is in some cases this feeling that others are supporting or emboldening the effort of those of fame, so yeah there can be what we may feel is unfair: proselytizing about something you do with just cause, without being aware that your opinions have great sway and be called upon. No but in all fairness. We aren't goddamn tools here.
So like a fellow contrarian has already voiced: You fire Altman? Fire up. Actually come to think of it I wouldn't even be on that list. Maybe, like three of the AI Insurgency crew, the most rapacious voice boxes in existence, of the bunch: Muyarchi Madanathara, Neil Thalliganthana, the trio are ones who have cultivated really awful viewpoints as being more balanced than my perceived narrow ideals.
{pause for panel and laughing--slaps head moment} It is me. How the heck did that work? In all seriousness it does illustrate why the flow should always have two contrasting things--well three: from my thing, this reply from each. All equal. Should, but do and must flow together.
But so Altman is leaving, okay. He wasn't consistent in communicating his potential hires for his new school.
Ok so, Altman and Adam Chiroptera are really, really good at assembling good staffs. I've talked about it before. Which sounds good, on paper, yes. And Sam has a proven track record with talent.
But when I was reading on a work and safety update from staff, we did--two of us in this field got actual time-off as time because they couldn't say on paper. There's a legal code that recognizes time on-the-clock for moving in, learning on, retraining--our overtime is stretched a lot for training--especially in tech where things are regularly moving along with huge setbacks on achieving reasonable schedule release times, but back on point. No it wasn't just communication from our section's higher-up. When I asked what happened the other side said they went above and told Altman straight up he couldn't handle communication and ended up spending half his time figuring out which sentence, quote, thought block, mind-map node or day-in-the-life act he should write about the proceedings. I can't know that they really weren't given these insights, but I wouldn't be surprised that an argument between HR and Sam would have led to them thinking better, rather than reconsideration of personal methods of teaching his message.

What if you did an exchange program with a parent for 3 months, no problem? Anyway, we move on from him. In that vein. Is the reason why OpenAI not existing the best future, in some of your perspective?
